content_of_post_to_answer: Does skipping the habit of getting dressed in the morning make you feel more productive during the rest of the day?
answer: Skipping the morning dressing routine can feel productive because it removes a small decision and lets you begin working without interrupting your momentum. But there's a subtle distinction between saving time and eliminating the psychological transition into the day. Getting dressed can signal that personal time has ended and focused work has begun. If you work better without that ritual, there's no reason to force it. Just make sure you're removing an unnecessary routine, not losing the boundary that helps you switch into work mode. Productivity depends less on what you wear than on how deliberately you begin.
